system_overview: This specification models the voucher redemption operation from RFC 3506, implemented using the Two-Phase Commit protocol. A Voucher Transaction Provider coordinates voucher holders and voucher collectors to atomically redeem vouchers, transitioning them from valid to redeemed status. Redemption represents the holder claiming the goods or services promised by the voucher.
actors_and_components: Four types of participants interact: (1) A Voucher Transaction Provider (the coordinator) managing the commit/abort decision. (2) Voucher Holders who present vouchers for redemption. (3) Voucher Collectors who fulfill the voucher's promise. (4) The vouchers themselves, transitioning from valid to redeemed. Communication uses a shared message pool.
state_variables: The system tracks seven pieces of state: (1) each voucher's current status (valid or redeemed), (2) each voucher's lifecycle phase (working or done), (3) each holder's participation state (holding, prepared, redeemed, or aborted), (4) each collector's participation state (waiting, prepared, redeemed, or aborted), (5) the coordinator's state (initial or done), (6) the set of participants from which the coordinator has received redemption preparation confirmations, and (7) the pool of all messages sent.
initial_state: All vouchers are in the valid state with lifecycle in the working phase (since redemption presupposes issuance). All holders are in the holding state. All collectors are in the waiting state. The coordinator is in the initial state with empty preparation confirmations and empty message pool.
actions: The coordinator can: receive preparation confirmations from a holder and a collector, redeem a voucher (transitioning it to redeemed and lifecycle to done, enabled only when all participants have prepared), or spontaneously abort. Each holder can: prepare for redemption (sending a preparation message), spontaneously abort, receive a redemption message (transitioning to redeemed state), or receive an abort message. Each collector can: prepare, spontaneously abort, receive a redemption message (transitioning to redeemed), or receive an abort message.
safety_properties: Type correctness ensures all variables remain in expected domains. A consistency invariant ensures no holder and collector reach conflicting decisions: a holder must not be redeemed while a collector is aborted, and a holder must not be aborted while a collector is redeemed.
model_bounds: The model-checking configuration uses three vouchers, three holders, and three collectors. Deadlock checking is disabled.
additional_assumptions: The specification imports and claims to implement the voucher lifecycle specification as a refinement. Messages accumulate in a set and are never consumed. Preparation messages from the coordinator are not explicitly modeled. The redemption operation requires the voucher to be in the valid/working state.
